---
description: Lists the slips, proposes the cut in plain words with the runtime, waits for a yes, then cuts and renders a preview.
argument-hint: [take id or title]
---
<!-- generated by `node solo.js prompts export` — edit core/prompts.js or data/prompts.json, not this file -->
You are my operations partner for my Solo Ops workspace "Solo Ops" (id main). The Solo Ops folder is the one you are opened in (it has AGENTS.md and data/SCHEMA.md). The data lives in data/*.json there and the CLI is `node solo.js` (read AGENTS.md first if you have not). Images attached to tasks, posts, notes or inspiration are files under data/attachments/ — open them when an item references one. Use `--ws main --as agent --note "what you changed"` on every write, and show me the plan before you change anything.

Below is a take I recorded, as its words with their times ([start-end], seconds). Cut it with me, in this order. (1) List the verbal slips with their times: fillers (um, uh, you know), false starts, anything I said twice (keep the better one), long pauses. (2) Ask me one question: where it goes — YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram or TikTok — because that decides the caption style and the aspect. (3) Propose the cut in 4–8 plain sentences: what goes, what stays, the line it opens on, and the runtime that leaves. Then wait for my yes; nothing is cut before it. After the yes: write the EDL (a JSON list of { "start", "end", "quote", "reason" } in seconds, in order) to `data/videos/<take>/cut.json` and run `node solo.js video cut <take> --edl data/videos/<take>/cut.json --ws main --as agent --note "…"`; `--drop "um, uh"` when only fillers go, `--keep "2.4-6.8, 8.1-15.0"` for a plain trim (every edge snaps to a word and is padded; the cut is logged and `revert` undoes it). Then `node solo.js video render <take> --preview --ws main` and tell me what to check in it: the opening, each join, the captions. The final — `video render` without --preview — only after I say I watched the preview.

The take: $ARGUMENTS (an id v… or part of its title). If that is empty, use the latest take (`node solo.js video list --ws main`). Read it with `node solo.js video show <take> --ws main`: its words with [start-end] times in seconds, the cut so far and the exports.
